title: Descend and glue already constructed local Zariski cokernels
statement: Let $T,c,G,I,U,K,J,d,q$ be as in [lem-trf-etale-presented-local-cokernels], and suppose the etale family $U_i\to T$ is jointly surjective. Fix any local recovery datum $L$ of that lemma: in particular its quasi-coherent modules $F_i$, comparisons $L_{U_i}F_i\simeq G|_{U_i}$ and normalized tensor coordinates are specified. In the coordinates [def-trf-etale-presented-recovery-coordinates], there exist unique overlap lifts on every etale test overlap, satisfying their section-image equations and cocycle. There exist a quasi-coherent Zariski module $F$, chart isomorphisms $u_i^*F\simeq F_i$ inducing those lifts, normalized linear tensor coordinates for $F$, and an isomorphism $L_TF\simeq G$ whose specified local equations hold and whose morphism is unique with those restrictions. This is the datum EtalePresentedDescentRecovery relative to L. The conclusion does not identify F with R_T G or assert any property of the adjunction counit.

proof.text: The pairwise and triple fibre products are objects of the small etale site by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. On $V_{ij}$, the modules $p_i^*F_i,p_j^*F_j$ are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. Use the etale restriction and composition identifications of [lem-trf-etale-extension-free-presentations-hom] to regard the restrictions of $b_i,b_j$ as maps from their respective $L_{V_{ij}}$-images to the same $G|_{(V_{ij})_{\mathrm{et}}}$. Fullness gives the unique lift $\phi_{ij}$ of $b_j^{-1}b_i$. Fullness also lifts its inverse $b_i^{-1}b_j$; faithfulness sends the two inverse equations back to the Zariski modules. Thus $\phi_{ij}$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Pull to $V_{ijk}$, using the composition identifications of [def-pc-module-pullback], preservation of quasi-coherence [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent], and restriction compatibility in [lem-trf-etale-extension-free-presentations-hom]. The $L_{V_{ijk}}$-image of the proposed cocycle equation is $(b_k^{-1}b_j)(b_j^{-1}b_i)=b_k^{-1}b_i$. Faithfulness gives $\phi_{jk}\phi_{ij}=\phi_{ik}$. Pulling this equation for $i=j=k$ along the small diagonal $V_i\to V_{iii}$ gives $e_i^2=e_i$ for $e_i=\Delta_i^*\phi_{ii}$. As $e_i$ is invertible, $e_i=1$. This is a normalized descent datum.

proof.text: The given family is a covering of the terminal object of $T_{\mathrm{et}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale] it is an fpqc covering in the family sense; no quasi-compactness of the individual $u_i$ is required. Apply clause (1) of [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] to the quasi-coherent $F_i$ and the datum of steps 3--4. It gives a quasi-coherent $F$ and isomorphisms $a_i:u_i^*F\simeq F_i$ satisfying $a_j=\phi_{ij}a_i$ on each overlap, with canonical pullback identifications understood.

source.place: Tag 03DX, proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent, proof of (2) by the same construction as (1).

proof.text: By the restriction compatibility of [lem-trf-etale-extension-free-presentations-hom], define $c_i=b_iL_{V_i}(a_i):(L_TF)|_{(V_i)_{\mathrm{et}}}\simeq G|_{(V_i)_{\mathrm{et}}}$. On overlaps, $c_j=b_jL(\phi_{ij})L(a_i)=b_j(b_j^{-1}b_i)L(a_i)=c_i$. Apply [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] on the small etale site at its terminal object to obtain the unique module map $b:L_TF\to G$ restricting to $c_i$. The inverses $c_i^{-1}$ also agree on overlaps and glue by the same lemma to a map $d:G\to L_TF$. The composites $db,bd$ restrict to identities, so the uniqueness clause of that lemma gives $db=1$ and $bd=1$. This constructs the required global isomorphism.
